name: sortable
title: Sortable
description: Reorder a list or grid by drag, keyboard and agents, built with definePrimitive over UI SDK's createReorder: a controlled string[] order, a draft while an item moves, an optional drag handle, checked items that move together, announcements with overridable labels, a FLIP slide on the motion tokens, and agent actions move(id, index) and reorder(order).
docs: `Sortable aria-label` holds `SortableItem value`s, rendered from its children function `({ order }) => …` so the items follow the draft while one moves; `value`/`defaultValue` and `onValueChange(order, details)` own the order (`details.reason` is `drag`, `move-key` or `imperative`, and `details.cancel()` or a controlled value that doesn't change keeps the old one). Without `handle` the root is a listbox and each item an option, one tab stop: arrows move focus, Space or Enter lifts the focused item, arrows, Home and End move it, Space or Enter drops it and Escape puts it back. With `handle`, the root is a list, each item a list item and its `SortableHandle` (named `labels.handle(label)`, a grip icon by default) the one tab stop and the drag target, so the item's own buttons stay clickable. `variant` is `card` (separate bordered items, the default), `row` (rows edge to edge in one bordered box) or `plain` (no surface); `orientation` is `vertical`, `horizontal` or `grid`. `selected` (or Ctrl/Cmd+Space and Ctrl/Cmd/Shift+click) checks items that move together; `disabledKeys` can't be picked up; `preview` drags a copy so a scrolling list neither clips the item nor grows, and scrolls near its edges (`autoScroll`); both are read on mount. Style from `data-moving`, `data-grabbed` (a pointer drag, translated by core's `--drag-x`/`--drag-y`), `data-checked` and `data-disabled` on items and `data-moving`/`data-dragging` on the root: nothing re-renders per pointer move. `labels` overrides the role descriptions, the handle's name, the keyboard instructions every item is described by and the announcements (English by default). Agents see the sortable by its label, with `move(id, index)` and `reorder(order)` and its items named by `itemLabel` or their text; `agentMoves={false}` hides them, for a host that offers its own confirmed action. `useFlip(ref, selector, trigger)` slides elements to their new places with the root's `duration-panel` and `ease-standard`, and does nothing under reduced motion.
